## Detector-aware quadratic error and compatibility

For fixed P, input PJ=J and g>=||QHP||, put L=integral g. Exact evolution satisfies ||QUJ||<=L and ||PUJ-U_PJ||<=L^2/2. If the declared CPTP output erases P/Q coherences, complete referenced half-diamond error is at most L^2. For the sine bath this becomes Lambda M, rather than sqrt(Lambda M) for the larger emitted-state task. It is unconditional, including the retained source and all classical records. Postselected normalization needs an acceptance denominator.

We resolved that obstruction by dilating collection before compression. Put Lf=(sqrt(E_0)f,...,sqrt(E_R)f), with E_0=I-sum E_r. Bosonic second quantization intertwines the original Weyl dynamics with its dilated version. Separate finite spaces in the orthogonal output ports commute with ideal photon counting even if the original collection effects do not commute.

For any N-mode original space W, choose W_r=sqrt(E_r)W. Total dimension is at most (R+1)N and total omitted mass is no greater. This bounds one-particle dimension, not Fock memory or runtime. The approximant may leave the original embedded subspace; the common-dilation channel comparison charges that difference. Existing coupling/collection kernels provide every port inner product. No independent-reservoir approximation is inserted.

The construction covers finitely many declared passive count ports/bins. Fully resolved continuous arrival-time records and phase-sensitive detection require further work. Coherent reuse of discarded fields changes the output task.
